summary: This informational memo defines an X.509 certificate extension that lets a certification authority state the warranty it offers for the certificate. It is meant to put warranty information in the certificate itself.

eli5.summary: A product can come with a warranty card. This lets a digital certificate carry a note saying how much the issuer will stand behind it.

questions: can a certificate state a warranty
how to add warranty to x.509 certificate
subtitle: Adding warranty information to X.509 certificates

tldr.problem: Certificate Authorities have no standard way to state the warranty they offer for a certificate, so relying parties cannot easily determine what financial protection or liability coverage they have if something goes wrong.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC defines a non-critical X.509 certificate extension that a CA can include to explicitly state the warranty offered: the validity period, the monetary amount, and whether claims are aggregated or per-transaction.
tldr.outcome: CAs can now embed warranty information directly in certificates, giving relying parties clear visibility into coverage and allowing automated risk decisions.

today: RFC 4059 is an Informational RFC and has not been obsoleted or updated. The warranty certificate extension it defines is available for use by CAs that wish to embed warranty information in their issued certificates.

sections.title: Introduction and Motivation
sections.content:
A digital certificate is a cryptographic credential issued by a Certificate Authority (CA) that proves someone's identity or right to perform an action. When a CA issues a certificate, it takes on some liability: if the CA is negligent and issues a certificate to an imposter, or if a private key is compromised, relying parties who trusted the certificate may suffer financial loss.

CAs can obtain insurance to cover this liability, just like product manufacturers. However, there was no standard way for a CA to communicate to certificate users what warranty or financial coverage it offers. Without explicit warranty information, relying parties cannot easily assess their risk or make informed decisions about whether to trust a certificate. This RFC defines an extension that lets a CA state its warranty directly in the certificate, making warranty information transparent and even automatable.
sections.eli5: When a bank gives you a certificate to prove you are who you say you are, sometimes they promise to pay if something goes wrong. But before this document, there was no standard way for them to state that promise in the certificate itself.

sections.title: Warranty Extension Structure
sections.content:
The warranty extension is a non-critical X.509 extension identified by the object identifier id-pe 16. It can contain either NULL (indicating no warranty) or a WarrantyData structure (indicating an explicit warranty).

The WarrantyData structure contains a base warranty (mandatory) and optionally an extended warranty and a URL pointing to warranty terms and conditions. Both base and extended warranty information use the same structure: WarrantyInfo, which specifies a validity period, a currency amount, and a warranty type (aggregated or per-transaction).
sections.eli5: The extension is simple: it either says "no warranty" or gives three pieces of information: how long the warranty lasts, how much money it covers, and whether the limit is total or per incident.

sections.title: Warranty Types and Currency
sections.content:
Two types of warranties are supported. Aggregated warranties set a ceiling on total claims: once fulfilled claims reach the warranty amount, no further claims are paid. Per-transaction warranties impose a limit on each individual claim, but each transaction is treated independently, so multiple claims can add up beyond the single transaction limit.

The currency amount is specified using ISO 4217 currency codes (such as 840 for US dollars). The amount is given as an integer with an exponent to indicate decimal placement. For example, $48,525.50 is encoded as: currency code 840, amount 4852550, and exponent 2 (meaning two decimal places). The warranty validity period can either match the certificate's validity period exactly, or be explicitly specified with its own notBefore and notAfter times. An optional URL can point to the full terms and conditions document.
sections.eli5: A warranty might say "we cover up to $10,000 total" (aggregated) or "we cover up to $10,000 per claim" (per-transaction). The extension also records which currency, when the warranty is valid, and where to read the full warranty terms.

sections.title: Deployment and Risk Assessment
sections.content:
When a CA includes warranty information in a certificate, relying parties can automatically assess financial protection. A system processing certificates can extract the warranty extension, determine coverage, and make decisions based on warranty presence and amount. A high-value transaction might require a certificate with substantial warranty backing, while low-risk operations might accept certificates with minimal or no warranty.

The warranty mechanism gives CAs tools to differentiate their offerings: CAs with insurance backing can advertise high-value warranties, while CAs with limited liability can offer low-value warranties or none. This enables market-based trust: applications and organizations can set their own policies about what warranty levels they require for different purposes, and CAs can compete on the coverage they offer. The extension is non-critical, so old software that does not understand warranty extensions can still process the certificate; it simply cannot see the warranty information.
sections.eli5: With warranty information in the certificate, a computer can automatically decide whether to trust it based on coverage. A bank might say "we only accept certificates with a $1 million warranty", and a system can check this automatically.
